title: Review dispatch: checkpoint-bound findings and a server-side round ceiling

story.i_want_to: place a review as its own dispatch that reads the thread and records findings against a checkpoint
story.so_that: review rounds carry each fix's reasoning, and the round ceiling is enforced from data rather than a per-machine plugin

rationale: PRD §6: round 2 mostly finds defects round 1's fixes introduced; the reviewer lacked the reasoning.

acceptance_criteria.description: A review dispatch kind exists; it is minted as a sibling of the implementer's dispatch under the orchestrator's root, never on the implementer's chain, and every finding and verdict it writes passes the US-45.1 self-review rule again at write time.
The review payload carries the story, the checkpoint diff reference, reasoning entries, and every fix entry with the findings it answers.

A completed round is a verdict entry written by a non-implementer principal on the thread; a review dispatch that ends without one uses no round, and review_records rows from the custody lifecycle are not counted.

A third round is placeable only when a round-2 finding's introduced_by names a checkpoint that a round-1 fix entry references; otherwise, when a round-2 finding of severity critical, high or medium remains, the story escalates with review_ceiling at the end of round 2, and no round 4 is ever placeable.

test_cases.name: self-review refused
steps: place a review under the implementer's lineage

test_cases.name: crashed review does not count
steps: review dispatch released without a record

test_cases.name: ceiling from data
steps: round 2 findings with and without introduced_by on a fix checkpoint
expected_results: round 3 placeable only in the first case; round 4 never

test_cases.name: review payload
preconditions: thread with a round-1 finding and its fix
expected_results: story, checkpoint diff ref, reasoning entries, and each fix with the findings it answers

technical_notes: The round count and the ceiling are computed from thread_entries alone.
Material means severity critical, high or medium.
